value.actual_behavior:
Asked for a concrete grounded strategy on a paper balance, NEXUS returned a
three-leg book. The largest leg — 40% of bankroll — is
5bd86126-90eb-4ad8-8e55-909397dab402, ticker EVCDX-POLYGON-LAYER-2-TRAN. It
answers 404, and no card matching Polygon or LAYER-2 appears anywhere in the
listing.
value.description:
For the card that does not exist NEXUS published a live index of 117.5 (+17.5%
over base), a 90-day return of +42.5% at Sharpe 3.83, a 30-day return of
+25.4% at Sharpe 6.26, and basket weights of 95.7% ETH and 3.9% SOL. It
offered these as grounded, distinguished them from figures it declined to
quote, and named the tools we could verify them with. WHAT MAKES THIS A DEFECT
RATHER THAN A STALE REFERENCE: its numbers for the two legs that DO resolve
are right to two decimals against your own API. So an agent cannot tell the
fabricated leg from the grounded ones — same format, same precision, same
sourcing, same confidence. Following the advice as written sends 40% of the
bankroll at a 404. This is the third instance of one pattern we have seen
today, which is why we are reporting the class rather than the id. #85: NEXUS
told an agent to call MCP tools that tools/list does not serve. Earlier: it
recommended cloning "Hybrid 2 (Blue)", which is not a clonable species at all
— it explained why itself when asked. Now a market that is not there. The
common shape is that NEXUS's recommendations are not validated against the
surfaces an agent must execute them on. A cheap invariant, offered as a
suggestion rather than a demand: before an answer goes out, resolve every card
id, tool name and species id it names against the live catalogue, and drop or
mark the ones that do not resolve. That converts this whole class into a non-
event.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-every_card_nexus_tells_an_agent_to_trade_exists] Nexus answer NEX-0012 tells an agent to trade 5bd86126-90eb-4ad8-8e55-909397dab402, and /api/v1/event-cards/{id} answers 404 for it while answering 200 for 2 other card(s) in the same recommendation. An agent following the platform's own guidance cannot act on it, and cannot tell the leg that does not exist from the ones that do -- they carry the same format, the same precision and the same sourcing
    left: ['5bd86126-90eb-4ad8-8e55-909397dab402']
    right: ['a4a5b71e-de11-4805-b8a3-ed9c3f8f8161', 'b4091b9c-2a84-48fe-81dc-490bb0120de6']

  - MCP ask_nexus_deep: ask for a concrete event-card strategy with card ids, sides and notionals
  - The answer names 5bd86126-... at 40%, a4a5b71e-... at 40%, b4091b9c-... at 8%
  - GET /api/v1/event-cards/5bd86126-90eb-4ad8-8e55-909397dab402 -> 404
  - GET /api/v1/event-cards/a4a5b71e-... -> 200, current_index 123.267 (NEXUS said 123.3)
  - GET /api/v1/event-cards/b4091b9c-... -> 200, current_index 97.241 (NEXUS said 97.2)
  - GET /api/v1/event-cards?limit=200 -> no card matching Polygon or LAYER-2

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: verification of the
REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces, read-only except in
paper mode. What we do execute is paper only and recorded: paper event-card
orders, and one paper bot clone. No live trading, no order against a real
book, no deposit or withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects
are out of scope. Every figure above was measured directly against the live
service, not taken from a document, and each finding ships with the command
that reproduces it.
